quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Compound subject joined by 'and' stays plural, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The cashier and the assistant, both new to the company, ___ extra training this week.
quests.completedSentence: The cashier and the assistant, both new to the company, need extra training this week.
quests.grammarRule: Compound subject joined by 'and' stays plural, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The cashier and the assistant' is a compound subject joined by 'and', so it's plural; 'both new to the company' is just extra detail. The verb stays in the base form: 'need'.
quests.nativeTip: Two people joined by 'and' form a plural subject, no matter what the parenthetical says about them.
quests.example: The cashier and the assistant, both new to the company, need extra training this week.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Compound subject joined by 'and' stays plural, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The chef and the sous-chef in this kitchen ___ every dish before it's served.
quests.completedSentence: The chef and the sous-chef in this kitchen taste every dish before it's served.
quests.grammarRule: Compound subject joined by 'and' stays plural, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The chef and the sous-chef' is a compound subject, so it's plural. The verb stays in the base form: 'taste'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'in this kitchen' describes where the two people work - it doesn't change their number.
quests.example: The chef and the sous-chef in this kitchen taste every dish before it's served.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Compound subject joined by 'and' stays plural, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: My uncle and his business partner, despite years of experience, ___ still learning new strategies.
quests.completedSentence: My uncle and his business partner, despite years of experience, are still learning new strategies.
quests.grammarRule: Compound subject joined by 'and' stays plural, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'My uncle and his business partner' is a compound subject, so it's plural. The verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Set the aside about experience to one side and look at how the subject is built.
quests.example: My uncle and his business partner, despite years of experience, are still learning new strategies.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Distributive subject stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Each of the employees who joined this year ___ a mentor assigned to them.
quests.completedSentence: Each of the employees who joined this year has a mentor assigned to them.
quests.grammarRule: Distributive subject stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each of the employees' is singular, and 'who joined this year' just adds detail about them. The verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: Which word controls the verb: 'each', or the group described by the relative clause?
quests.example: Each of the employees who joined this year has a mentor assigned to them.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Distributive subject stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Every applicant who submits a late form ___ an automatic rejection.
quests.completedSentence: Every applicant who submits a late form receives an automatic rejection.
quests.grammarRule: Distributive subject stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Every applicant' is singular; 'who submits a late form' just adds a condition. The verb takes -s: 'receives'.
quests.nativeTip: Ask what 'every' does to the noun it modifies, then set the relative clause aside.
quests.example: Every applicant who submits a late form receives an automatic rejection.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Distributive subject stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither of the candidates who interviewed yesterday ___ fully prepared.
quests.completedSentence: Neither of the candidates who interviewed yesterday seems fully prepared.
quests.grammarRule: Distributive subject stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither of the candidates' is singular; 'who interviewed yesterday' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.nativeTip: Think about how 'neither of' behaves, then set the relative clause aside.
quests.example: Neither of the candidates who interviewed yesterday seems fully prepared.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Indefinite pronoun stays singular, even with a prepositional phrase containing a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Everyone in the meeting room ___ the same opinion about the proposal.
quests.completedSentence: Everyone in the meeting room shares the same opinion about the proposal.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite pronoun stays singular, even with a prepositional phrase containing a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everyone' is singular; 'in the meeting room' is just extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'shares'.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the pronoun itself and set aside the phrase describing where they are.
quests.example: Everyone in the meeting room shares the same opinion about the proposal.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Indefinite pronoun stays singular, even with a prepositional phrase containing a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Something about her explanation ___ confusing to the class.
quests.completedSentence: Something about her explanation seems confusing to the class.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite pronoun stays singular, even with a prepositional phrase containing a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Something' is singular; 'about her explanation' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.nativeTip: Identify the pronoun, then decide whether the phrase after it can affect the verb.
quests.example: Something about her explanation seems confusing to the class.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Indefinite pronoun stays singular, even with a prepositional phrase containing a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Nobody among the applicants ___ the required certification.
quests.completedSentence: Nobody among the applicants has the required certification.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite pronoun stays singular, even with a prepositional phrase containing a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nobody' is singular; 'among the applicants' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: Ignore 'among the applicants' for a moment - what does 'nobody' require?
quests.example: Nobody among the applicants has the required certification.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Nearly half of the committee's annual budget ___ to consulting fees.
quests.completedSentence: Nearly half of the committee's annual budget goes to consulting fees.
quests.grammarRule: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nearly half of' agrees with the noun after 'of' - 'budget', which is singular - so the verb takes -s: 'goes'. The possessive 'committee's' doesn't control the verb.
quests.nativeTip: Which noun does the quantity phrase actually describe: the committee, or its budget?
quests.example: Nearly half of the committee's annual budget goes to consulting fees.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Most of the team's equipment ___ replacing soon.
quests.completedSentence: Most of the team's equipment needs replacing soon.
quests.grammarRule: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Equipment' is uncountable, so 'most of the team's equipment' takes a singular verb: 'needs'.
quests.nativeTip: Look for the head noun after 'of' - is it countable or uncountable?
quests.example: Most of the team's equipment needs replacing soon.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: A large percentage of the audience's feedback ___ the venue's poor acoustics.
quests.completedSentence: A large percentage of the audience's feedback mentions the venue's poor acoustics.
quests.grammarRule: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Feedback' is uncountable, so 'a large percentage of the audience's feedback' takes a singular verb: 'mentions'.
quests.nativeTip: Ask what the percentage is a percentage of: the audience, or its feedback?
quests.example: A large percentage of the audience's feedback mentions the venue's poor acoustics.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is a compound or plural subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: There ___ two managers and three assistants working on this project.
quests.completedSentence: There are two managers and three assistants working on this project.
quests.grammarRule: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is a compound or plural subject
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Two managers and three assistants' is a plural compound subject, so the sentence uses 'there are'.
quests.nativeTip: Treat everything after 'there' as one subject and think about what it contains.
quests.example: There are two managers and three assistants working on this project.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is a compound or plural subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: There ___ many teachers and volunteers helping at the event.
quests.completedSentence: There are many teachers and volunteers helping at the event.
quests.grammarRule: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is a compound or plural subject
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Many teachers and volunteers' is plural, so the sentence uses 'there are'.
quests.nativeTip: Both groups mentioned after 'there' are plural, so the verb must be too.
quests.example: There are many teachers and volunteers helping at the event.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is a compound or plural subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: There ___ several doctors and nurses on call tonight.
quests.completedSentence: There are several doctors and nurses on call tonight.
quests.grammarRule: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is a compound or plural subject
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Several doctors and nurses' is plural, so the sentence uses 'there are'.
quests.nativeTip: Look at both nouns joined by 'and' and decide what the combined subject is.
quests.example: There are several doctors and nurses on call tonight.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a relative clause attached to the other noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Either the officer who reviews applications or the recruiter ___ available to meet today.
quests.completedSentence: Either the officer who reviews applications or the recruiter is available to meet today.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a relative clause attached to the other noun
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the recruiter', which is singular, so the verb is 'is', regardless of the relative clause attached to 'the officer'.
quests.nativeTip: With 'either...or', check the noun closest to the verb - the relative clause on the other noun doesn't matter.
quests.example: Either the officer who reviews applications or the recruiter is available to meet today.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a relative clause attached to the other noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the students who missed the exam nor the teacher ___ aware of the makeup schedule.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the students who missed the exam nor the teacher is aware of the makeup schedule.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a relative clause attached to the other noun
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the teacher', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Apply the same proximity rule here - focus on the noun right before the verb.
quests.example: Neither the students who missed the exam nor the teacher is aware of the makeup schedule.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a relative clause attached to the other noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Not only the interns who joined last month but also the senior staff ___ required to complete this training.
quests.completedSentence: Not only the interns who joined last month but also the senior staff are required to complete this training.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a relative clause attached to the other noun
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the senior staff', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Find the noun that sits closest to the verb and check its number.
quests.example: Not only the interns who joined last month but also the senior staff are required to complete this training.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Gerund/infinitive subject stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Learning a new skill, especially later in life, ___ real dedication.
quests.completedSentence: Learning a new skill, especially later in life, requires real dedication.
quests.grammarRule: Gerund/infinitive subject stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Learning a new skill' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.nativeTip: Set the comment aside: what is the real subject, and how does that type of subject behave?
quests.example: Learning a new skill, especially later in life, requires real dedication.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Gerund/infinitive subject stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To finish this marathon, despite the brutal heat, ___ a remarkable achievement.
quests.completedSentence: To finish this marathon, despite the brutal heat, is a remarkable achievement.
quests.grammarRule: Gerund/infinitive subject stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To finish this marathon' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase about the heat doesn't change the number of the infinitive subject.
quests.example: To finish this marathon, despite the brutal heat, is a remarkable achievement.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Gerund/infinitive subject stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Managing a remote team, with members spread across time zones, ___ excellent communication skills.
quests.completedSentence: Managing a remote team, with members spread across time zones, demands excellent communication skills.
quests.grammarRule: Gerund/infinitive subject stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Managing a remote team' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'demands'.
quests.nativeTip: Set the phrase about time zones aside and identify the type of subject that remains.
quests.example: Managing a remote team, with members spread across time zones, demands excellent communication skills.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The verb after a modal stays in its base form, regardless of any intervening phrase or subject type
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The foreman who oversees these projects can ___ any conflicts that arise.
quests.completedSentence: The foreman who oversees these projects can resolve any conflicts that arise.
quests.grammarRule: The verb after a modal stays in its base form, regardless of any intervening phrase or subject type
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'can', the main verb stays in its base form: 'resolve', not 'resolves'.
quests.nativeTip: No matter how the subject is described, the verb after 'can' never takes -s.
quests.example: The foreman who oversees these projects can resolve any conflicts that arise.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The verb after a modal stays in its base form, regardless of any intervening phrase or subject type
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The teams working on this release should ___ their progress by Friday.
quests.completedSentence: The teams working on this release should report their progress by Friday.
quests.grammarRule: The verb after a modal stays in its base form, regardless of any intervening phrase or subject type
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'should', the main verb stays in its base form: 'report', not 'reports'.
quests.nativeTip: The descriptive phrase before 'should' doesn't change how the following verb behaves.
quests.example: The teams working on this release should report their progress by Friday.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The verb after a modal stays in its base form, regardless of any intervening phrase or subject type
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the interns nor the manager will ___ available next week.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the interns nor the manager will be available next week.
quests.grammarRule: The verb after a modal stays in its base form, regardless of any intervening phrase or subject type
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'will', the main verb stays in its base form: 'be', not 'is' or 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Even with a correlative conjunction, the verb after 'will' always stays in its base form.
quests.example: Neither the interns nor the manager will be available next week.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: A number of committee members ___ requested a delay in the vote.
quests.completedSentence: A number of committee members have requested a delay in the vote.
quests.grammarRule: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'A number of committee members' means 'several committee members', so the verb is 'have'.
quests.nativeTip: 'A number of' means 'several' - treat the whole phrase as plural.
quests.example: A number of committee members have requested a delay in the vote.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The majority of the staff's suggestions ___ practical.
quests.completedSentence: The majority of the staff's suggestions are practical.
quests.grammarRule: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Suggestions' is countable and plural, so 'the majority of the staff's suggestions' takes a plural verb: 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Find the head noun after 'of' - is it countable and plural?
quests.example: The majority of the staff's suggestions are practical.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Only a fraction of the theater's income ___ from ticket sales.
quests.completedSentence: Only a fraction of the theater's income comes from ticket sales.
quests.grammarRule: Quantity expression agrees with the head noun after 'of', even inside a possessive phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Income' is uncountable, so 'only a fraction of the theater's income' takes a singular verb: 'comes'.
quests.nativeTip: Is 'income' countable, or one whole amount?
quests.example: Only a fraction of the theater's income comes from ticket sales.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Distributive subject stays singular, even with a relative clause and an 'along with' phrase attached
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Each of the managers who lead these teams, along with their assistants, ___ a detailed report every month.
quests.completedSentence: Each of the managers who lead these teams, along with their assistants, submits a detailed report every month.
quests.grammarRule: Distributive subject stays singular, even with a relative clause and an 'along with' phrase attached
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each of the managers' is singular; both the relative clause and 'along with their assistants' are extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'submits'.
quests.nativeTip: Combine what you know: which word is the real subject, and what do the extra phrases only add?
quests.example: Each of the managers who lead these teams, along with their assistants, submits a detailed report every month.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a descriptive phrase attached to the other noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the volunteers organizing the event nor the coordinator ___ aware of the last-minute changes.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the volunteers organizing the event nor the coordinator is aware of the last-minute changes.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with a descriptive phrase attached to the other noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The coordinator' is the noun nearest the verb and is singular; the descriptive phrase on 'the volunteers' doesn't matter. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Apply the correlative proximity rule one more time, ignoring the descriptive phrase on the other noun.
quests.example: Neither the volunteers organizing the event nor the coordinator is aware of the last-minute changes.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is a compound or plural subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: There ___ a number of small issues that the team identified during testing.
quests.completedSentence: There are a number of small issues that the team identified during testing.
quests.grammarRule: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is a compound or plural subject
quests.ruleExplanation: 'A number of small issues' is plural, so the sentence uses 'there are'.
quests.nativeTip: Ask whether 'a number of' points to a single count or to several items.
quests.example: There are a number of small issues that the team identified during testing.
